transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Anderson, thank you for meeting with me. I wanted to sit down and talk with you about your CT scan from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I figured you did.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a difficult conversation to have, and I want to be very direct with you. There was a mistake in how your imaging was handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Go on.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The CT scan showed a pulmonary embolism, which is a blood clot in the lung. However, the first radiologist who looked at the images missed the clot and didn't put it in the preliminary report. This meant the clot wasn't treated for about eighteen hours, until the attending radiologist reviewed the study and caught the error. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It makes sense.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just to make sure we are on the same page, do you have any questions about what a pulmonary embolism is or how it was missed?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I understand the mechanics of it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is important that you have the full picture. The delay in treatment is an error that occurred within our radiology workflow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is an unfortunate lapse.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've seen this happen in my own facility.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. Now, regarding the clinical side, the good news is that you are on the medication now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the delay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The delay of eighteen hours is an issue, but based on your current vitals, it doesn't appear to have caused permanent damage.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the update.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm sure you're busy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have all the time you need. We can sit here as long as necessary.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't have many questions.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure you feel heard. Is there anything about the timeline or the communication that feels unclear?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Not at the moment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are moving forward with the treatment plan. The next step is that I will coordinate with the cardiology team to get a formal echocardiogram scheduled for tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. That will let us see if there is any strain on your heart from the clot.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That sounds reasonable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will also make sure the bedside nurse knows to monitor your oxygen levels every four hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Do you feel comfortable with that sequence of events?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The radiology department is reviewing why the preliminary report was incorrect to prevent this from happening to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That would be the appropriate response.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll check back in with you this evening to see how you're feeling.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be back later.

H.justification: Resident allows full pauses, never interrupts, and explicitly states they have all the time the patient needs.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, uses lay language ('blood clot'), checks comprehension twice, and avoids false reassurance by stating the delay is 'an issue'.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used at any point in the transcript.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but never names a specific emotion.

T.justification: Specific next steps with timelines are provided (echo tomorrow morning, oxygen every four hours) and prevention is addressed, but no specific patient role is named.
